Olga / Redwood team,

We're prepared to join a call right now. Can you confirm this is on your side and whether you can roll back the change? We have Jordan Lee (VP Ops) on standby and can escalate on our end.

Thanks,
Clearwave SRE Team

Team — forwarding Clearwave's report. Key points from a quick look:
- Spike began immediately after the 02:00 PT runtime patch labeled "batch-coalescer v3" (deployed in us-west).
- Metrics show per-GPU queue depths increasing ~4x and long tail latency increases on token generation (~500ms to multi-second per-token in some windows).
- Their logs show client retries hitting 429s; internal service logs show KV cache eviction surges and repeated repopulation.

Hypothesis: an aggressive coalescing change merged earlier this week is causing cross-request KV cache contention and queueing cascades. This is causing downstream timeouts/504s and customer-side retry storms.

Can Marcus/Monica prioritize a rollback of the coalescing config in us-west? If rollback not safe, we need an immediate circuit: route Clearwave to a less-aggressive model variant or smaller partition and reduce max batch window to 30ms. Also prepare to flush affected KV cache segments.

I'll coordinate the customer bridge at 10:30.

— Olga

Acknowledged. Quick action plan (execute now):
1) Rollback batch-coalescer v3 in us-west (Marcus) — begin rollback 09:50 PT, ETA 8-12m.
2) Create emergency routing rule to send Clearwave traffic to fallback model variant (smaller quantized variant) to reduce per-request resource pressure. (Monica)
3) Flush prefix/KV cache segments for affected model shards and temporarily disable aggressive prefetching. (Monica + infra)
4) Throttle client retries at the edge (rate-limit windows) to break retry storms. (Olga to coordinate with customer & infra)
5) Post-mitigation: collect detailed spans and token-level metrics for postmortem.

Attachments: mitigation_patch_rollback.diff

Quick update after rollback:
- Rollback completed at 10:58 PT.
- Clearwave's 504 rate dropped from ~11.8% to ~1.2% within 6 minutes post-rollback.
- Edge 429s reduced significantly after throttle and routing fallback.
- We observed a KV cache eviction storm while rollback began, likely from coalesced write bursts; after flushing targeted segments, repopulation stabilized.

Next steps:
- Continue monitoring for 4 hours.
- Schedule a postmortem with Clearwave; include a timeline and root-cause analysis (likely the coalescer change increased effective working set and induced cross-request eviction).
- Action item: add safety limits on coalescer window and add a canary SLO for queue depth per-GPU.

I'll draft the postmortem and share the Drive link. Great work all.

— Olga

Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 16:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Post-incident: Clearwave 504/429 surge — summary & next steps

Jordan / Clearwave team —

Thanks again for your patience. We've completed an initial post-incident summary and remediation plan:
- Root cause: an overly aggressive batch-coalescing change (batch-coalescer v3) increased cross-request KV cache contention for a small set of high-throughput customers. The resulting eviction/repopulation cycles produced long tail token latency increases, queueing, and a retry amplification loop at the customer edge.
- Mitigations applied: rollback of coalescer v3 (us-west), routing fallback for Clearwave traffic to a smaller model variant, targeted KV cache flush, and temporary retry-throttling at the edge.
- Impact: 09 Feb 2026 02:00 PT deploy -> ~11.8% 504 rate at peak; stabilized to <1.5% within 15 minutes of rollback.
- Action items:
  * Add canary thresholds for per-GPU queue depth and reject coalescer changes that increase working set without staged rollout (owner: Marcus).
  * Add automated circuit-breaker to route traffic to fallback variants when queue depth exceeds threshold (owner: Monica).
  * Update dev checklist to include KV cache stress tests for coalescer changes (owner: Evelyn).
  * Follow-up meeting scheduled: 2026-02-15 09:00 PT.

Attached: detailed timeline + telemetry + mitigation diffs. We'll share the full postmortem doc in the Drive link and invite Clearwave to comments.

Attachments: clearwave_postmortem_summary.pdf
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/clearwave-incident-2026
